# How to Use AI Overviews in Google Drive on Your Phone

Ever opened the Drive app, typed a search term, and then spent minutes scrolling through a dozen PDFs to find the bit you need? With AI Overviews, you can see a concise summary right at the top of your results, saving you time whether you're juggling personal projects or work files.

## What you'll need before you start

- **The latest Google Drive app** installed on your phone (Android or iOS).
- **A Google account** signed in. Personal Gmail works for most people. Google Workspace users may need their admin to turn on Gemini features.
- **Access to Gemini** (Google's large language model — think of it as the engine that writes the summaries). Some Workspace plans need the Gemini add-on, which is a paid extra.
- **At least a few documents in Drive** so the AI has something to summarise. New or empty accounts won't have anything to show.

If you're on a personal Gmail account in Australia, you should see the feature without extra setup. Workspace users: ask your IT admin if Gemini is enabled for your account.

## Step 1 — Update the Google Drive app

Open the **Google Play Store** (Android) or **App Store** (iOS) and search for "Google Drive". If you see an **Update** button next to the app, tap it. If it says **Open**, you're already on the latest version.

This matters because AI Overviews is being rolled out gradually — older versions of the app don't include the feature, so an outdated install is the most common reason people can't find the toggle.

💬 Example: Search the store for "Google Drive" and look for an **Update** button.

**You'll know it worked when:** the app's version number on the store page is current (check the "What's new" section dated within the last few weeks).

## Step 2 — Turn on AI Overviews in Settings

Open the Google Drive app and tap the **hamburger menu** — that's the three horizontal lines in the top-left corner of the screen. Scroll down and tap **Settings**, then look for an option called **AI features** (or similar wording such as "Google AI in Drive"). Tap the **AI Overviews** toggle so it switches to **On**.

If you don't see an "AI features" entry, your account may not have Gemini access yet, or your organisation's admin hasn't enabled it.

💬 Example menu path: **☰ → Settings → AI features → AI Overviews (On)**

**You'll know it worked when:** the toggle is coloured and sits in the "On" position, and you get a small confirmation message.

## Step 3 — Run a search that triggers an Overview

Go back to the main Drive screen and tap the **search bar** at the top. Type a term that matches something you've actually stored — a project name, a client, a topic, or a date. Then tap **Search** on your keyboard.

Drive returns matching files as usual, but with AI Overviews enabled, an **AI Overview** card appears at the very top of the results, above the file list. If the card doesn't appear, try a broader search (e.g. just one keyword) or a query that matches multiple files.

💬 Example search: **"project proposal 2024"** or **"meeting notes March"**

**You'll know it worked when:** you see a card labelled "AI Overview" sitting above the list of files, with a short paragraph of text inside it.

## Step 4 — Read the summary and check the sources

Tap the **AI Overview** card to expand it. You'll see a short paragraph that pulls together key points from the matching documents, plus small source references underneath — tap one to open the file the AI used.

Read the summary as a starting point, not as gospel. A **large language model (LLM)** — think of it as the AI's brain, predicting text based on patterns it's learned — can occasionally get details wrong, so always open the original file if a number, date or name matters.

💬 Example: tap a source labelled **"Project_Proposal.pdf"** to verify the AI's claim against the actual document.

**You'll know it worked when:** you can tap a source, jump straight into the matching PDF or Doc, and confirm the summary lines up with what's on the page.

## Step 5 — Ask a follow-up question

Beneath the summary, there's a field labelled something like **"Ask a question"** or **"Ask about these files"**. Tap it and type a follow-up. The AI replies in a short answer, again using only the files in your search results.

This is where the feature really shines — instead of opening five PDFs, you can interrogate them in plain English.

💬 Example prompts you can copy:
- *"What are the main milestones?"*
- *"Which document mentions the budget?"*
- *"Summarise the action items for next week."*

**You'll know it worked when:** the AI replies with a direct answer that mentions a document you have stored, and tapping the source takes you back to that file.

## Common mistakes

- **The "AI features" option is missing from Settings.** Fix: your Google account may not have Gemini access. Personal Gmail accounts in Australia usually do; Workspace accounts need the Gemini add-on enabled by your admin. Also make sure the app is fully updated.
- **No AI Overview card appears after searching.** Fix: try a broader query that matches several files, not a specific filename. AI Overviews only generate when the AI has multiple relevant documents to summarise.
- **The summary gets a fact wrong.** Fix: this is called a **hallucination** — when an AI confidently makes something up. Don't trust the summary for exact numbers, dates, or names; always tap a source reference to verify before you act on it.
- **The app is on the latest version but the toggle is greyed out.** Fix: sign out of the app, restart your phone, and sign back in. If it's still greyed out, the feature hasn't rolled out to your region yet — Google's release is gradual.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: you can locate recipes, warranty info, or school assignment details in seconds, freeing up time for the things you enjoy.
- **For work or study**: AI Overviews let you skim multiple documents at once, making report writing or project planning faster and less stressful.
- **If you're just getting started**: try a simple search like "budget spreadsheet", read the AI-generated paragraph, then click a file if you need more detail. You'll quickly see how the feature saves clicks.

## Wrap-up

AI Overviews turn a long list of Drive files into a single, readable snapshot, so you spend less time hunting and more time doing. Update your Drive app, turn on AI Overviews, and try a search for something you already have stored. In a few taps, you'll experience a smoother, smarter way to work with your own documents.
